vedic_reference.note: Rooted in Sanskrit and Vedic mythology, Surendra is the name of the lord of the ocean, Lord Indra, who is considered the king of gods in Hinduism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Surendra reflects the Hindu mythological belief in a supreme deity who possesses unfathomable power and control over all aspects of creation. This concept is prevalent within Indian culture, where the deity is revered and revered devotionally for his strength, courage, and the ability to grant people their desires and wishes - opening doors to victory and success in their lives.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Surendra is a reminder of an essential connection that exists between an individual and the divine deity - signifying the inherent inner strength and the ultimate cosmic power. Through the name, one can seek to overcome their inner weaknesses and fears while trusting in the protective and empowering guidance of a higher power to navigate through life's challenges. In essence, it serves as a spiritual beacon, offering hope, courage, and the assurance of ultimate victory when faced with adversity.

historical_references.reference: Surendra was a king of the Solar Dynasty, who ruled over the region of Haihayas in central India. He is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. According to legend, he was a powerful and just ruler, who was respected by his people and was a friend to the Pandava brothers.

Surendra was also the name of a king of Bengal who ruled during the 13th and 14th centuries. He is known for his military prowess and is said to have expanded the borders of his kingdom significantly during his reign.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
